title: Missing moeb tool: run_command (generic shell execution)
description: Every run that verifies compilation or tests is forced to use the external Bash tool because no moeb-native shell execution tool exists. This has produced 14 distinct occurrences across 9 separate signals, all of which collapse to the same root gap. Narrow language-specific tools (cargo_build, cargo_test) were considered but rejected: moeb is project-agnostic, so baking in Rust-specific tooling would require parallel npm_test, pytest, go_test, etc. tooling indefinitely. A generic run_command tool is the correct abstraction. The security concern around arbitrary shell execution is not a meaningful objection — the orchestrating agent already has Bash access through the MCP session; run_command does not expand the blast radius, it merely routes the call through moeb's tool registry.
proposed_resolution: Implement a run_command(command, cwd?, timeout_ms?) moeb tool in Rust that executes a shell command via std::process::Command and returns { stdout, stderr, exit_code }. The tool must be registered in both the CLI tool registry and the MCP stdio server tool list to satisfy kernel-thin-and-parity. Platform shell dispatch (PowerShell on Windows, sh on Unix) should be a decision record in the spec.
